title: Hermit HLS / long-running transcode design — StartFfMpeg + segment serving

part1_seam_extension.goal: Add ONE long-running, segment-producing spawn method behind a seam so all orchestration is unit-testable with a fake, and only the real tokio::process spawn is ffmpeg-gated/coverage-carved.
part1_seam_extension.decision: Add a NEW sibling trait `SegmentTranscoder` in hermit-mediaencoding (NOT a method on the existing probe-only `Transcoder` — probes return captured output; a long-running job returns a live handle, so keeping them separate keeps each trait honest and object-safe). The existing `Transcoder` (get_process_output/get_process_exit_code) is untouched.

new_trait.definition: #[async_trait] pub trait SegmentTranscoder: Send + Sync { async fn start_transcode(&self, req: &SpawnRequest) -> Result<Box<dyn TranscodeChild>, String>; }

fields: arguments: Vec<String>     // fully-built ffmpeg args (from encoding_helper); Vec<String> not a single string so the fake and the real spawn agree on tokenization
output_dir: PathBuf        // the per-session segment cache dir; created by orchestration BEFORE calling the seam
log_path: PathBuf          // FFmpeg.Transcode-*.log target (stderr is streamed here)

handle_type.name: TranscodeChild
handle_type.definition: #[async_trait] pub trait TranscodeChild: Send + Sync { fn has_exited(&self) -> bool; fn exit_code(&self) -> Option<i32>; async fn wait(&self) -> i32; async fn kill(&self) -> Result<(), String>; }
notes: has_exited()/exit_code() are the sync polls StartFfMpeg + GetSegmentResult read in their wait loops (mirror TranscodingJob.HasExited / ExitCode).
wait() awaits process exit (drives the OnFfMpegProcessExited equivalent — flips has_exited, records exit_code).
kill() is the SIGKILL/Process.Stop equivalent used by KillTranscodingJob.
Object-safe: `_assert_object_safe` fn on both traits, like the existing traits.

concrete_impl.name: TokioSegmentTranscoder
concrete_impl.behavior: start_transcode spawns tokio::process::Command(program).args(arguments).current_dir(working_dir).stdin(piped).stderr(piped); wraps the Child in TokioTranscodeChild that stores an Arc<AtomicBool> exited + Arc<Mutex<Option<i32>>> exit_code, spawns a task that pipes stderr->log_path and awaits child.wait() to set those, and holds the kill sender.
concrete_impl.coverage: This ONE module (the spawn + child wrapper) is the un-mockable real I/O. It is exercised ONLY by the ffmpeg-gated integration test (part5). It is carved out of the unit-coverage gate (part-coverage_carveout).

fake_for_tests.name: FakeSegmentTranscoder
fake_for_tests.behavior: start_transcode writes N fake segment files (hls{index}.ts etc.) into output_dir on a schedule (or immediately), returns a FakeTranscodeChild whose has_exited/exit_code are script-controlled. Lets every orchestration path (segment-exists / wait-for-segment / kill / cleanup / failed-start) run deterministically under unit tests with zero ffmpeg.

part2_streamstate_job_shape.reuse: EncodingJobInfo/BaseEncodingJobOptions in encoding_helper/transcode_state.rs already carry the arg-builder subset (output_file_path, transcoding_type, run_time_ticks, media_source, output_container, live_stream_id via base_request). Extend minimally rather than a new type.
additions_to_StreamState: segment_length_secs: i32   // state.SegmentLength — segment cut length; drives GetCommandLineArguments and the segmentGapRequiringTranscodingChange = 24/segment_length heuristic
wait_for_path: Option<PathBuf> // state.WaitForPath — the exact segment file StartFfMpeg blocks on before returning
segment_container: Option<String> // state.Request.SegmentContainer — 'ts' | 'mp4'; default '.ts' (get_segment_file_extension already ports this)
play_session_id: Option<String>, device_id: Option<String> // needed to register the job + kill by session

TranscodeJob_request.note: The registry already has TranscodingJobHandle (play_session_id, path, job_type, device_id). StartFfMpeg produces one of these AND needs the live child + a cancel flag. Introduce an internal RunningJob (owned only inside the impl, NOT in hermit-traits):
RunningJob_fields: output_dir: PathBuf     // segment cache dir to delete on kill (DeleteHlsPartialStreamFiles)
TranscodeJob_request.carries_from_request: media source path (state.media_source / output_file_path), fully-built ffmpeg args (from encoding_helper GetCommandLineArguments/GetProgressiveVideoFullCommandLine), output/segment dir, play-session-id, segment container, job_type (Hls|Progressive).

part3_startffmpeg_orchestration.location: New method on TranscodeManagerImpl (or a StartFfMpeg free fn taking &impl SegmentTranscoder + &TranscodeManagerImpl). Depends ONLY on the SegmentTranscoder seam + filesystem, so it is fully unit-tested with FakeSegmentTranscoder.
part3_startffmpeg_orchestration.signature: pub async fn start_ffmpeg(&self, transcoder: &dyn SegmentTranscoder, state: &StreamState, output_path: &Path, args: Vec<String>, job_type: TranscodingJobType) -> Result<TranscodingJobHandle, String>
steps: 2. (AcquireResources / attachment extraction / user-permission check are DEFERRED — noted; software path only for v1)
3. Build SpawnRequest { program = media_encoder.encoder_path(), arguments = args, working_dir, output_dir = directory, log_path }
4. register the job in the registry FIRST (OnTranscodeBeginning) so a concurrent segment request finds it; register_job(handle) already exists
5. child = transcoder.start_transcode(&req).await? ; on Err -> on_transcode_failed_to_start (remove job) and return Err
6. store RunningJob { handle, child, output_dir, playlist_path, segment_extension }

7. AWAIT-UNTIL-SEGMENT-EXISTS: let target = state.wait_for_path.unwrap_or(output_path); loop { if target.exists() || child.has_exited() { break } sleep(POLL_INTERVAL_MS=100).await } with an overall TIMEOUT (WAIT_FOR_FILE_TIMEOUT_MS, default 30000 — NEW setting candidate; C# loops unbounded on the CTS, we add a bound to avoid a hung request)
8. if child has_exited && exit_code != 0 -> Err(ffmpeg exited with code N)
9. (StartThrottler/StartSegmentCleaner are DEFERRED — flagged; not needed for first correct playback)

segment_cache_dir_strategy.root: server transcode path (ServerConfigurationManager.GetTranscodePath()) — reuse the configured cache path; DeleteEncodedMediaCache clears it on startup (port later).
segment_cache_dir_strategy.per_session: playlist file lives at <transcode_root>/<hash>.m3u8; segments are <transcode_root>/<hash>{index}.<ext> (mirror GetSegmentPath: folder + filenameWithoutExt + index + ext). The 'hash' is Jellyfin's deterministic output-file id (StreamingHelpers) — port the id derivation so a re-request reuses the same dir/playlist (enables OnTranscodeBeginRequest reuse instead of respawn).
segment_cache_dir_strategy.wait_until_segment_N: GetSegmentPath(state, playlist, index) => folder.join(filename + index + ext). 'Segment N ready' = file exists AND (child.has_exited() OR segment N+1 exists) — port GetSegmentResult verbatim; poll every 100ms until cancel/exit.

cleanup.kill: kill_transcoding_jobs already removes from registry + notifies SessionReporter. Extend the impl so kill also calls child.kill().await and (when delete_files) removes every file in output_dir whose name contains the playlist stem (DeleteHlsPartialStreamFiles). This filesystem delete moves behind the existing SessionReporter.on_job_killed seam OR a small FileCleaner seam so it stays unit-testable with a temp dir.
cleanup.ping_timeout: PROGRESSIVE_PING_TIMEOUT_MS=10000 / HLS_PING_TIMEOUT_MS=60000 already ported. The actual kill-timer task (OnTranscodeKillTimerStopped) is the remaining piece: a tokio task per job that fires kill when now-last_ping >= ping_timeout. Unit-test with a fake clock / manual tick.

settings_candidates_to_raise_with_user: WAIT_FOR_FILE_TIMEOUT_MS (default 30000) — how long StartFfMpeg blocks for the first segment before erroring
SEGMENT_READY_POLL_INTERVAL_MS (default 100) — GetSegmentResult / StartFfMpeg poll cadence (C# hardcodes 100)
segmentGapRequiringTranscodingChange divisor 24 (C#: 24/segment_length) — the max forward gap before respawn

part4_api_endpoints.note: All endpoints below are currently 501 stubs in hermit-api. This design WIRES them; they are this phase's scope, NOT the later portable-TODO phase.

endpoints.does: build master playlist listing the variant (main.m3u8) stream(s) — DynamicHlsHelper.GetMasterPlaylist; no transcode spawn, just StreamState + playlist text
the VOD variant playlist — DynamicHlsPlaylistGenerator::create_main_playlist (ALREADY DONE in hermit-hls). Just adapt StreamState->CreateMainPlaylistRequest and return the string.
GetLiveHlsStream: event playlist; spawns ffmpeg (StartFfMpeg) then WaitForMinimumSegmentCount(minSegments) then returns live playlist text

GetDynamicSegment: the core segment endpoint — if segment file exists serve it (OnTranscodeBeginRequest); else lock, decide startTranscoding (currentTranscodingIndex null / requested<current / gap>24/len), KillTranscodingJobs+DeleteLastFile if respawn, StartFfMpeg, then GetSegmentResult (wait-until-ready loop) and stream the .ts/.mp4
HlsSegmentController: ValidateTranscodePath (path-traversal guard) then serve from transcode dir; OnTranscodeBeginRequest/OnTranscodeEndRequest around the response

endpoints.route: GET /Videos/{itemId}/stream.{container} (+ the transcode branch of /Videos/{itemId}/stream, already partly done for direct-play)
endpoints.does: Progressive transcode: if not direct-play, GetProgressiveVideoFullCommandLine -> StartFfMpeg (Progressive) -> stream the growing output file (ProgressiveFileStream). Direct-play + Range is already implemented.

trait_calls: TranscodeManager::kill_transcoding_jobs (extended to kill child + delete files)

endpoints.does: audio HLS: same machinery as video but audio-only StreamState (GetMasterHlsAudioPlaylist/GetVariantHlsAudioPlaylist/GetHlsAudioSegment)

GetUniversalAudioStream: decide direct-play (static file) vs 302 redirect vs transcode-to-HLS (delegates to the audio master.m3u8 path). First-light can implement direct + redirect; HLS branch reuses the audio HLS machinery.
AttachmentExtractor::get_attachment(item_id, media_source_id, index) -> stream bytes with the attachment's mime; already have the trait, needs the concrete extractor + handler wiring

part5_integration_tests.location: crates/hermit-mediaencoding/tests/segment_transcode_ffmpeg.rs (integration dir → NOT part of the unit-coverage gate)
part5_integration_tests.gating: Each test starts with: if std::env::var('HERMIT_FFMPEG_TESTS').is_err() { eprintln!('skip'); return; } and also which('ffmpeg')/which('ffprobe') guard. So absent-ffmpeg CI is green; the gate runs only when the env is set on a host with ffmpeg.
plan: 1. generate a tiny clip: ffmpeg -f lavfi -i testsrc=duration=6:size=128x72:rate=10 -f lavfi -i sine=frequency=440:duration=6 -c:v libx264 -c:a aac /tmp/clip.mp4 (in a #[ctor]-style once, or per-test in a tempdir)
2. build real ffmpeg HLS args (mpegts, -hls_list_size 0, -hls_playlist_type vod, output <dir>/out%d.ts + out.m3u8) via encoding_helper or a fixed arg vector
4. run start_ffmpeg orchestration with wait_for_path = out0.ts; assert it returns Ok and out0.ts exists and is non-empty
5. child.wait().await == 0; assert out.m3u8 parses (contains #EXTM3U, #EXT-X-ENDLIST, >=1 #EXTINF) and at least 2 .ts segments exist
6. mp4/fmp4 variant: assert out-1.mp4 init segment + out0.mp4 appear; version 7 playlist
7. kill test: start a longer transcode, child.kill().await, assert has_exited() and (with delete) segment files removed
8. failure test: bogus args -> exit_code != 0 surfaces as Err from start_ffmpeg
part5_integration_tests.excluded_from_unit_gate: tests/ integration tests never count toward `cargo llvm-cov` unit lines; additionally the concrete TokioSegmentTranscoder module carries the coverage carve-out (part-coverage_carveout) so the crate stays >=80% unit.

coverage_carveout.target: The single module crates/hermit-mediaencoding/src/transcoding/tokio_segment_transcoder.rs (real tokio::process spawn + Child stderr-pump/wait/kill wrapper).
coverage_carveout.mechanism: Module-level `#![cfg_attr(coverage_nightly, coverage(off))]` (matching the hermit-traits definitions-crate exemption precedent) scoped to just this file, plus adding the file to a documented carve-out note. Everything else (SpawnRequest build, start_ffmpeg orchestration, wait-until-segment loop, GetSegmentResult ready logic, kill/cleanup, playlist adapters, all API handlers' non-ffmpeg logic) is unit-tested via FakeSegmentTranscoder and stays counted.
coverage_carveout.record_in: brain/DEFERRED.md — add a row under the HLS/transcode entry noting the tokio_segment_transcoder carve-out + the HERMIT_FFMPEG_TESTS integration gate, mirroring the existing Transcoder-seam rationale.

part6_portable_todo_routes.explanation: Of the 194 still-501 routes, the subsystem-deferred ones (LiveTv, Plugins/Packages/Repositories, SyncPlay, Intros/IntroSkipper, Channels, Backup, Trickplay tiles, RemoteSearch providers, FallbackFont, FileTransformation, SkipButtonCss, Tmdb, OpenSubtitles plugin) are NOT portable-TODO — they are whole missing subsystems. The HLS/streaming routes are THIS design's scope (part4). The remainder below are self-contained, in-model, portable handlers for a later phase — grouped.
part6_portable_todo_routes.note: The virtual-folders / library-folders group borders on a subsystem (library management); listed as portable because the handlers are CRUD over already-ported library models. Confirm scope when the phase starts.
